brief: This is a Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities chart-pack (Johannes Duttenhoefer, 5 Oct 2026): a sequence of standalone chart captions across many unrelated subjects, with no connecting argument. It reports that US-listed ETF inflows have topped $1.5trn this year, already beating last year's full-year record after only three quarters, with average daily inflows over $8bn and GS expecting full-year 2026 flows to surpass $2trn; cybersecurity ETFs are on track for one of their best inflow months (+$950m). Market breadth has plunged and the share of negative-beta stocks has risen, as in the Tech Bubble; US large-cap dominance exceeds Europe's, and the top 10 US companies dominate world equity market cap. Consensus expects S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth of 27% y/y (9% for the median stock), with the forward P/E back near its 10-year average. Hyperscaler cloud revenue backlogs are growing and capex is seen up over 100% y/y, weighing on free-cash-flow yield; data-center GPU power demand is forecast to grow at a 62% CAGR to 2030. France's bond spreads have widened sharply. European banks have outperformed the Magnificent 7 since 2022. Robot shipment forecasts are seen quadrupling, and seniors are set to dominate developed-market demographics.
